1.explanation:
• Slider.js – needs to short-circuit onDragStart, onKeyDown, onChange (and any other interactive handlers) when props.readOnly is true, just like it does for props.disabled, and ensure the readOnly flag is passed through so the container gets the .bx--slider--readonly class.

• _slider.scss – the read-only design requires hiding the thumb, preventing pointer events on the track, and styling the text input as read-only. We must add a .bx--slider--readonly selector with the CSS rules from the spec.

• Slider-test.js – add a Jest/RTL unit test that renders <Slider readOnly /> and asserts that the root element has the bx--slider--readonly class, and that interactive handlers are disabled.

• Slider-test.e2e.js – add an end-to-end test that mounts the read-only slider in the browser, attempts to drag the handle or type into the input, and verifies that nothing changes, and the .bx--slider--readonly class is present.
1.bug_scenario: When a consumer renders <Slider readOnly />, the slider is still fully interactive (you can still drag the thumb, keyboard controls still work) and the component does not pick up any of the read-only styles shown in the design spec (the thumb should disappear, the track should be non-interactive, the number input should render as read-only). In addition, there are no unit or E2E tests asserting that passing the readOnly prop adds the proper CSS class or disables interaction. To meet the acceptance criteria we need to treat readOnly like disabled in the event handlers, add the .bx--slider--readonly styles in the SCSS, and add tests verifying the new class and behavior.

2.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Slider/Slider.js
   • We need to extend `render()` so that when `readOnly` is true, the thumb (`.bx--slider__thumb`) is not rendered or is hidden, and event handlers for drag/start/keydown are disabled.  
   • We must preserve the text input but only allow viewing (no dragging or arrow-key value changes).

2. packages/react/src/components/Slider/Slider.stories.js
   • Add a dedicated “Read-Only (Default Copy-Paste)” story for quick usage, and ensure the Playground story exposes `readOnly` in `argTypes` so that users can toggle it.

3. packages/react/src/components/Slider/Slider.test.js
   • Add RTL tests that render `<Slider readOnly>` and assert that the wrapper has the `--slider--readonly` class, that the thumb is absent or hidden, and that mouse/key events do not fire `onChange`.

4. packages/carbon-components/scss/components/slider/_slider.scss &
   packages/carbon-components-react/scss/components/slider/_slider.scss
   • In both Sass sources, add rules for `.bx--slider--readonly`:
     – hide or remove the thumb pseudo-element
     – adjust track/fill styling to be a static bar
     – style the text input box around the value per the token specs (border-strong, transparent background, typography)
     – ensure no hover/focus/active states appear on the track or handle.

These changes together will bring the read-only slider in line with the visual designs and accessibility requirements described in the bug report.
2.bug_scenario: In the current implementation, passing the `readOnly` prop to the `<Slider>` component correctly renders an un-editable `<input>` and applies the `--slider--readonly` CSS class, but it does not yet visually match the design spec for a read-only slider: the handle (thumb) remains visible and persistent slider interactions are still registered. In the design, a read-only slider should suppress the thumb, eliminate drag/key events on the track, and surface only a styled, non-interactive text box showing the current value.
